descriptionChirho: Qal: to be or become bitter in taste or experience, describing an inherent quality of bitterness.
Piel transitive: to make someone's life bitter, to attack or treat someone with bitterness and hostility.
Piel intensive intransitive: to experience or express intense bitterness, especially in bitter weeping.
Hifil finite: to cause something to become bitter, to make a situation or experience bitter.
Hifil specialized sense: to rebel or act defiantly, related to provoking bitterness through contention (cf. Meribah).
Hifil infinitive used adverbially: denoting the manner of intense bitter mourning or weeping.
Hitpael reflexive: to become enraged or deeply embittered within oneself, expressing internal fury or indignation.
